findings.note: Because shape and outline both denote 'fixed boundary,' gust:outline and drizzle:shape are each true 'lacks' relations, so a player could solve this swapped grouping just as validly as the intended one. Both halves read as: "gust necessarily lacks an outline (no fixed boundary)" and "drizzle necessarily lacks a shape (no fixed boundary), reading right half as drizzle:shape".
Not sure which word in each pair represents the 'full' concept and which the 'faint' one, or if the pairing itself is even correct.

notes:
set-distinctive-nonpart uses near-synonymous absence properties (shape/outline), letting the pairs be validly swapped or crossed; needs new word(s) with a clearly distinct, non-synonymous absent property.
- set-distinctive-nonpart: Shape and outline are near-synonyms for 'fixed boundary,' so gust:outline / drizzle:shape reads equally valid as the intended pairing, creating an accidental alternate solution and unclear ordering.
  Try: Replace one pair with a property that is not synonymous with the other's: e.g., keep gust:shape, change drizzle:outline to drizzle:weight (drizzle, like gust, necessarily lacks weight as a graspable quantity) — pick a property clearly distinct in meaning from 'shape'
  Or: Replace both pairs with words whose absent properties are unambiguous and non-overlapping, e.g., echo:shadow (no shadow) and gust:weight (no weight), avoiding any boundary/outline-type synonyms
  Or: Keep gust:shape but replace drizzle/outline entirely with a pair like smoke:texture (smoke has no fixed texture), ensuring the two absent properties are not synonyms of each other
Do not change: set-agent-instrument, set-attachment, set-enabling-agent — no allowlisted finding touches them.

persisted.note: Flipping the right pair to tassel:loop gives 'item fastens at point' on both sides (strap on a handle, tassel on a loop), so a player could solve this the 'wrong' way. Both halves read as: "item fastens at this point (strap : handle)" and "item hangs from this point, read as tassel : loop".

Mist is also weightless and drizzle also lacks fixed shape, so flipping the right pair to drizzle:shape gives the same 'diffuse thing lacks property' relation on both sides. Both halves read as: "phenomenon lacks this property (mist : weight)" and "phenomenon lacks this property, read as drizzle : shape".
